_comment: Per-route payload ledger. Enforced by scripts/check-route-budget.mjs in the docs build (blocking in CI via docs-build). Fails when a route EXCEEDS its budget and when it drops far enough below that the budget has gone stale — see that script's header, and engineering/decisions/2026-08-17-studio-dynamic-loading-audit.md §9.7. COVERS ALL FIVE ROUTES perf-nightly.yml measures, as of 2026-09-05: the three content routes joined when `script-size` was deleted from that nightly for measuring what happened to LOAD rather than what the build produced (35% of 150 repeat readings of an IDENTICAL commit moved past its own 3% tolerance, worst 106KB on a ~200KB page). See engineering/decisions/2026-09-02-alarm-channel-saturation.md.
_units: bytes. eagerJsGz = gzip(level 6) of every /_astro/*.js referenced in the route's HTML. htmlRaw = the HTML document itself. Budgets USUALLY carry ~3% headroom above the measured build — the `studio` route deliberately does not, and its _eagerJsGzNote says why: at this route's weight 3% is ~20KB of silent headroom on the one route this ledger exists to watch. Read the per-route note before assuming the convention; the gate also fails if a route drops more than 5% BELOW its budget, which means the number here is stale and must be ratcheted down.

684400 -> 693900 (2026-09-21): narration EXPLANATION, re-measured on the tree rebased onto c3540d6 — the THIRD time on this branch, because `main` has moved under it twice more and this budget describes the MERGED tree or it describes nothing. 691610 bytes gz across 84 chunks, +7210 over the budget it replaces. The two deltas are NOT separable by arithmetic and no attempt is made to pretend otherwise: bundlers dedupe across chunks, so two changes that each cost X do not cost 2X together, and adding this branch's standalone figure to main's does not reproduce the total. Attributed at the source: read-along-core.generated is the only bundle carrying narration. Nothing was found to give back — the kernels are heavily commented and the generated bundle carries ZERO comments, because esbuild strips them regardless of `minify: false`. THE FIFTH ROUND'S FIXES ADD TO IT AND THE NUMBER SAYS SO: the content-column nesting rule, the `cutOff` set and its clause, and the `keyInPills` flag are all new code on this route. SET TIGHT (+0.33%), the same margin and the same reason as the entries below. PREVIOUS: 682800 -> 684400 (2026-09-21): the `topic` anchor's track override became the `_track` DIRECTIVE, and the deck linter that coaches the migration is bundled eagerly on this route (PR #2257). MEASURED AS A PAIR, same machine, same toolchain, both trees rebuilt before the reading: base 498b3e6 = 681,673 bytes gz; this branch = 682,967. The branch costs +1,294, chunk count unchanged at 84. THE GATE WENT RED ON A REBASE, for the third time. `main` moved four times under this branch and twice raised this same ratchet for its own growth, so the number is attributed here rather than to whichever push happened to find the wall. An earlier raise on this branch was DROPPED in a rebase because #2272 raised the same field concurrently; this is not a second raise stacked on that one. TWO REDUCTIONS WERE ALREADY TAKEN and are not available again. `renderedBody` reached for `maskInert`, which dragged the whole HTML tokenizer onto this route: -1,571 gz, replaced by a local mask. And the lint rule was rewritten from a MODEL of markdown-it's `html_block` rule into a strict SUBSET of it, which is smaller as well as more correct - headroom went UP on that commit. What remains is `lib/core/track-spec.js`, the grammar kernel both render arms and the linter share (dropping it from one of them reopens the two-arm split the PR exists to close), plus the two rules. SET TIGHT at +1,433 bytes over the reading (+0.21%), the convention the last four entries used rather than the ~3% in _units: 3% of slack absorbs drift silently until one change finds the wall, and the change that finds it is not the one that spent the room - which is what happened here three times. The new number restores roughly the 1,127 bytes the route had on the base. AND THE ~900-BYTE CI OFFSET RECORDED BELOW DOES NOT HOLD ON THIS RUNNER. That note says a local pass under ~1KB of headroom is not evidence CI will pass. On this branch CI matched the local reading on seven consecutive heads and passed this gate at 170, 151 and 99 bytes of headroom. Trust CI's reading on the head. PRIOR: 681300 -> 682800 (2026-09-21): the shared
walker moved onto the real tokenizer, and `split-sections.js` is bundled for this route. `lib/core/top-level-h2.js` was ALREADY here (via lint-core -> topic-track and via masthead.transform, both on main: `CLOSED_BY_SIBLING` appears 3x in authoring-core.generated.js before this change), so none of the growth is the tokenizer module arriving — it is the new code. The bytes are the rewritten walk, `findClassAttr`/`withClass` (the attribute-position read and rewrite that replaced a regex over the whole open tag), and `scanTags`' quote-at-value-start and closed-rawtext-only fixes. NOT GIVEN BACK, and the give-back that looked obvious was checked and came back at exactly 0: splitting `scanTags` into its own module so this route could take the tokenizer without the element-stack walker buys nothing, because the whole module is already here for two other reasons. What is left is the fix itself — the old walk lost EVERY slide of a deck whose body merely mentioned a `
` tag, and the first cut of the new one lost every slide of a deck containing an apostrophe in an unquoted attribute; both measured at 0 of 3 slides stamped on a real render. Shrinking `findClassAttr` is the only remaining candidate and it is the piece an independent checker found the regex version getting wrong, so it is not where to buy 369 bytes. SET AGAINST THE LOCAL READING, WHICH IS THE CI READING THIS TIME: the ~896-byte CI offset the entry below records did NOT reproduce here — CI measured 665.7KB (681676 bytes) and this sandbox measures 681669, eight bytes apart. 682800 clears it by ~1.1KB (+0.17%), matching this route's deliberate tightness rather than the ~3% in _units. This branch found the wall once already — an earlier version of this entry raised to 697000 (+3%) before that pattern was visible in two consecutive entries. REGENERATE THE BUNDLES BEFORE YOU MEASURE. A first attempt reverted only `docs/src` and read the regression as ZERO, because `docs/src/playground/*.generated.js` still carried the branch's Cadenza — the measurement said 'not this PR's fault', and it was wrong. The growth is the normalizer that runs on every narration: ranges, ISO dates, clock times, ordinals, decades, ranks, versions, the bn/MM magnitudes, the bracketing peel and the status marks, plus cursor.align's preconditions. Not given back, because giving it back means a deck reads ($4.2M) as glyphs and $1 as 'one dollars'. Two candidates were checked for free bytes and both came back at exactly 0: voiceLanguageMismatch and validateTrack already tree-shake out of this route. Every other slide surface on this site renders inside a srcdoc iframe, and Readability (Firefox Reader View and its shake-to-summarize, and the reading modes Safari and Chrome ship) only ever reads the top-level document — measured on the built site, the hydrated /studio held 0

and 1118 characters of text, all of it chrome. Measured exactly, by building this route twice off one tree: 673454 bytes gz without the shell wiring, 673980 with it — +526, chunk count 82 -> 84. NOT GIVEN BACK, and one failed attempt is worth recording so nobody repeats it: factoring the two full-view branches (Fabricate, Article) into one shared frame component made it WORSE by 78 bytes — minification already collapses that duplication and the extra component costs more than it saves. THE NUMBER DELIBERATELY DEVIATES FROM THE ~3% IN _units. The convention would put this near 695KB (the CI reading x1.03), which opens ~20KB of silent headroom on the one route this ledger exists to watch — the route that grew 615KB -> 976KB with nothing noticing. 676000 is set instead to clear the EXPECTED CI reading (673980 local plus the ~896-byte CI offset recorded below, so ~674876) with about 1.1KB to spare.
